key_insight: Including non-forward scattering makes neutrino many-body evolution deviate from kinetic theory by changing both the timescale and the long-time behavior, revealing more non-classical dynamics than the truncated picture.
engineering_relevance: The paper quantifies quantum-computing resource costs for neutrino simulation, showing that efficient fermion-to-qubit encodings and circuit design are critical to keep entangling and non-Clifford gate counts manageable.
method: Compare a quantum kinetic model with a collision term against a full neutrino-neutrino many-body Hamiltonian
Study a simple dense neutrino-gas setup to isolate non-forward scattering effects
Estimate Trotter error scaling and circuit resource requirements for truncated vs full Hamiltonians
evidence_signal: The abstract reports qualitative comparison results and resource estimates, finding that full-Hamiltonian simulations require more resources than truncated models and that neutrino many-body simulation sits low for HEP but mid-to-high for quantum chemistry.
watch_item: Results are based on a simplified neutrino-gas model, so real astrophysical environments may introduce additional correlations, geometry, and scaling challenges.
paper_title: Collective neutrino oscillations: Many-body non-forward effects and non-classicality
